event.summary: Old tmux terminals lose access and work under the explicit migration policy
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: an update removes access to old terminals and their retained screens, and ends the programs still running there. Details: the assigned patch deletes the tmux terminal variant, discovery and resolution, including the former resolve_terminal_inner tmux branch (parent terminals.rs:973–1004); the replacement at terminals.rs:242–247 resolves host tabs only and agent_terminal:263–274 serves host handles only. This is intentional specification acceptance, not a proposed fix. Suggested bucket: highest if treated as a defect, because processes and retained terminal work are lost; could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed from the patch and pinned specification; startup implementation still to be checked for the migration premise. proposed_drop: explicit acceptance in SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 3006–3016: "This release ends them: the first time a host's supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program." The same paragraph says "one whose agent had already ended keeps its outcome, but its terminal's last screen, which lived in the server, is gone; old tabs are closed." SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, lines 2882–2888 also explicitly says the old terminals are ended and the driver is gone. possible_cover: those exact pinned specification sections. Caveat: this record covers the authorized migration loss itself, not unintended destruction of host terminals or unsafe cleanup; those require separate source checks. No runtime execution or observed behavior.

event.summary: Removing tmux sinks does not remove host-stream viewer isolation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether deleting the per-session sink lifecycle could let a stalled viewer freeze an agent or another session. Details: assigned patch lines 1071–1146 begin removal of the tmux sink constants and shutdown machinery. The replacement attachment path at service/handlers.rs:1914–1945 starts a GridStream over the already-driven HostTerminal. GridStream::catch_up at service/grid_stream.rs:427–460 and 475–484 takes owned snapshots through read_home, and read_home:524–560 finishes the emulator read before returning or waiting on status. GridStream::send:818–831 waits only on the viewer writer queue and its own pause/stall path; it neither suspends the terminal-host connection nor holds the emulator read across that wait. Thus the tmux sink's purpose has no remaining tmux output client to protect. SPEC.md Terminal experience:3031–3038 requires that no new-terminal viewer slow its agent; SPEC_impl.md Grid streams:3106–3122 describes the independent viewer pause. Suggested bucket if real: high/material UX, not highest; could-be-highest: no established loss-of-work or security route. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the deletion concern. proposed_drop: source refutation, independent runtime plus owned grid snapshots preserve the relevant isolation. possible_cover: none. No runtime behavior observed. This does not claim a full independent audit of grid output or host runtime internals.

event.summary: Host-only resolution retains exact selector and exited-tab boundaries
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether deleting tmux discovery and splitting agent lookup from tab lookup could redirect a stale tab selector into the agent, bypass retired-session refusal, or expose a finished tab as live. Source refutes those resolver routes: service/terminals.rs:231 preserves require_active_launch before either branch; :232–247 sends only Agent to agent_terminal, looks up Tab exclusively by that session cell and exact id, returns NotFound on absence and rejects finished tabs for LiveOnly. DeadIncluded is used only by resolve_terminal_for_close (:136–141). The parent host-tab branch at terminals.rs:899–912 has the identical active-launch guard, session-cell lookup and finished predicate; this comparison establishes that the surviving host behavior is preserved, not merely that a possible defect predates this commit. The removed tmux fallback is not replaced by an agent fallback. Related caller check: handlers.rs:2060–2083 ignores failed resolution and checks both channel and owning connection under the attachment lock before resizing. Suggested bucket if such misrouting existed: high/material UX, with potential highest only if wrong-target input or cleanup destroyed work; could-be-highest: yes as a considered consequence, but no shipped wrong-target route is established. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of these exact resolver hypotheses, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation at the cited selector/guard branches; no specification exception or parent drop is assumed. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this is not an independent certification of all host attribution, process cleanup, or stream inputs. Neighbour findings about hidden old-tab Delete consent and gone-host cleanup are distinct and are not refuted by this resolver check.
